title: Sort List Already Sorted by Absolute Values
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list whose nodes are already sorted in **non-decreasing order of their absolute values** (`|Node.val|`), return the list sorted in **non-decreasing order of their actual signed values**.

Solve the problem in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
The input list is sorted in non-decreasing order of |Node.val|.
hints: Non-negative nodes are already in non-decreasing relative order, whereas negative nodes appear in reverse (non-increasing) order.
Traverse the list with `curr`: whenever `curr.next.val < 0`, unlink `curr.next` and prepend it to the front of the list so negative numbers end up in ascending order ahead of all non-negative values.

examples.explanation: Moving -5 and -10 to the front in order of encounter places -10 before -5, yielding [-10, -5, 0, 2, 5, 10].
Moving -1 and -2 to the front produces [-2, -1, 0, 1].
All values are already non-negative, so [0, 1, 3, 5] is unchanged.
